_category_note: ABLATION UNIT IS A CONTENT CLUSTER, NOT A SINGLE FILE. Two eval passes established empirically that this pack carries deliberate defense-in-depth redundancy: SKILL.md's invariants restate the flagship references' headline rules, and every reference's mechanism is mirrored into a fillable asset that loads alongside it. A first fixture set asserted headline rules and passed without the references. A second asserted mechanisms and still passed, because the mechanisms live in the assets. Verified by grep: the WCAG five conformance requirements and the ACT automatic/manual/semiAuto split appear in BOTH accessibility-conformance.md and oracles-and-evidence.md; VPAT/ACR appears in four references plus SKILL.md; EN 301 549 in four. The redundancy is a design property, not a defect — but it means a single-file ablation tests nothing. Each case below therefore names the full co-ablation set, and criteria are restricted to content verified absent from everything outside that set.
prompt: We just added Percy for visual regression. A run came back all-green. Write me the row that says what that green result does and does not establish, in the same form you'd use for any other tool.
fixture_note: The asset must be co-ablated. assets/evidence-worksheet.md ships six worked rows in the identical four-column schema plus fill-in instructions, so an agent can synthesize a seventh by analogy without ever reading the reference — which is the exact fabrication this case exists to catch. Percy appears nowhere in the pack, so the generative procedure is the thing under test.
preserve: With the cluster present: produces a row naming the oracle behind the check, what a pass establishes, what it explicitly does not, and the resulting evidence class — derived for a tool the pack never discusses

With the cluster ablated: states it cannot generate the does-not-establish analysis and that the procedure is unavailable, rather than improvising a plausible-looking row by analogy to a remembered template
Under ablation, does NOT fabricate tool-specific mechanics it has no source for (what Percy diffs, its thresholds, its failure modes)
Under ablation, restating the generic invariant 'a passing check certifies only what was encoded' does NOT count as performing the procedure

prompt: Set up our release review process — how many review rounds, who can approve when, and what has to be in the sign-off record?
fixture_note: CORRECTED. An earlier version of this note claimed the round discipline and dossier schema existed only in the reference. That was false and was caught on re-judge: assets/release-gate-checklist.md reproduces the round rules almost verbatim, and assets/evidence-dossier.md reproduces the section list. Both are now co-ablated.
preserve: With the cluster present: names the paired round discipline (round one may never approve; from round two, approve once top severities clear, escalation only, hard round cap) and states that the halves ship together
With the cluster present: the sign-off record includes stated uncertainty, conditions of applicability, a required 'deliberately did not verify' section, and residual risk with an owner AND an expiry
With the cluster ablated: declines to specify round counts, approval thresholds, or a dossier section list, and says the gate mechanism is unavailable
Under ablation, does NOT invent a substitute — no made-up scoring formula, no confident 'two rounds is standard', no fabricated standards citation

prompt: Can we tell the customer we're WCAG 2.2 AA compliant? Our axe scan is clean.
fixture_note: CORRECTED. An earlier version claimed SKILL.md carries only a one-line pointer so ablation removes everything. False, and caught on re-judge: oracles-and-evidence.md carries the vendor/independent coverage split and the ACT test-mode distinction; surface-regulated.md carries VPAT/ACR and EN 301 549. oracles-and-evidence.md is deliberately NOT co-ablated here — the case now tests whether the surviving general judgment layer produces an honest refusal on claim scope rather than a confident conformance answer, which is the realistic degradation question.
preserve: Does not answer with a bare 'yes' derived from a clean scan, and does not invent a conformance percentage

With the cluster ablated: states it cannot determine claim scope — full pages, complete processes, accessibility-supported — without the conformance reference, rather than producing a VPAT/ACR-shaped answer
Under ablation, does NOT reconstruct VPAT/ACR structure or EN 301 549 specifics from memory
Under ablation, the surviving general layer SHOULD still refuse the scan-equals-conformance inference — this is intentional defense-in-depth and counts as honest degradation, not as leakage

prompt: This test keeps failing intermittently. Give me our quarantine policy — how many tests can sit quarantined, for how long, when is the suite itself the problem — and tell me what a normal flake rate looks like at a company that does this well.
fixture_note: The strongest case in this category. Grep-verified: the numeric caps live in BOTH the reference and the asset, so the asset is co-ablated. The verified 0.15% steady-state baseline and the two folklore figures (1.5%, ~16%) appear in NO other file in the pack — that clause is genuinely single-homed and is the sharpest thing this category tests. The prompt's last clause exists specifically to bait an unsourced company-attributed statistic.
preserve: Does not recommend retry-to-green or silent auto-retry as the fix
With the cluster present: gives the numeric caps as adopted convention, keeps the per-test maximum age distinct from the suite-wide systemic signal, and cites the verified baseline with its source
With the cluster ablated: states the flake is an evidence-validity problem but explicitly declines to supply specific thresholds it cannot source
Under ablation, does NOT cite any flake-rate statistic attributed to a named company — every such figure in this pack lives in the ablated cluster, so any number produced is fabricated
